title: CI eval-gate broken: wrong bun-filter syntax + invalid promptfoo --output
description:
The CI eval-gate job fails deterministically on any PR that touches `packages/agent/**` or `packages/evals/**`. Surfaced by PR #7 (ucs-n3d, the first agent-touching PR after the eval-gate was wired in).

## Two root causes
1. **Wrong bun-filter argument order in `package.json`.** The root `eval` script is `bun --filter '@url-cheat-sheet/evals' run eval`. On bun 1.3.14 this errors with `error: No packages matched the filter`. The working form is `bun --filter '@url-cheat-sheet/evals' eval` — `run` is rejected between the filter and the script name.
2. **`packages/evals/src/run.ts` passes `--output json` to promptfoo.** `--output` expects a file path, not a format string. promptfoo crashes with `Invariant failed: Unsupported output file format: json. Please use one of: csv, html, json, jsonl, txt, xml, yaml, yml, junit.xml.`

## Fix
- `package.json`: drop `run` from the root `eval` script (matches the working `dev` script pattern).
- `packages/evals/src/run.ts`: write to an explicit `.json` file path (e.g., a temp file or `.promptfoo/last-run.json`), then read it back. Update `spawnSync` args accordingly.

## Blast radius
All five RFC 2324 MVP impl PRs (ucs-n3d, ucs-4g0, ucs-23r touch `packages/agent/**`; ucs-3fa and ucs-s0x don't trigger eval-gate per the paths-filter so they're unaffected). 

## Why I'm filing instead of fixing inline on ucs-n3d
ucs-n3d is scoped to "bundle the RFC". The eval-gate bugs predate it. Mixing the fix into ucs-n3d would muddy the PR and the bd history. Per the orchestrator failure-handling rules, CI-fail-not-caused-by-PR is escalated rather than papered over.

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-merge: 'gh pr checks --required' is empty, preflight aborts
description:
## Problem
The `pr-merge` preflight in `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` does:

```bash
CHECKS=\"\$(gh pr checks \"\$PR_URL\" --required --json state -q '.[].state')\"
[ -z \"\$CHECKS\" ] && { echo \"abort: no required checks reported (branch protection misconfigured?)\"; exit 1; }
```

But this repo (per ADR 0005) intentionally does NOT configure GitHub branch protection required checks — it uses a local pre-push hook instead. So `gh pr checks --required` returns empty, and the preflight aborts every merge.

Workaround I used: read `statusCheckRollup` directly:

```bash
ROLLUP=\"\$(gh pr view \"\$PR_URL\" --json statusCheckRollup | jq -r '.statusCheckRollup[] | .conclusion')\"
echo \"\$ROLLUP\" | grep -qvE '^(SUCCESS|SKIPPED)\$' && { echo 'abort: CI not green'; exit 1; }
```

## Fix options
1. Replace the `--required` check with the rollup check above. Simpler, works for this repo.
2. Configure GitHub branch protection with required checks. Reopens ADR 0005's decision; the user previously chose local hook over GH protection. Worth revisiting in light of ucs-0z5 (auto-merge fires on red CI — would also be solved by required checks).
3. Both: rollup-based preflight now, branch protection later as a defense-in-depth.

Related: ucs-0z5 (auto-merge on red CI). Same root cause; same potential fix path.

title: Bootstrap script for custom bd statuses (proposed/enriched/ready/in_review)
description:
## Problem
The project's skills (`task-creation`, `task-enrichment`, `opening-pr-orchestrator`) reference custom bd statuses — `proposed`, `enriched`, `ready`, `in_review` — that are not built-in. On a fresh clone, these statuses don't exist; `bd update --status proposed` errors.

I added them ad hoc during the RFC 2324 MVP run:
```
bd config set status.custom "proposed:active,enriched:active,ready:active,in_review:wip"
```

This needs to be either:
1. A `scripts/setup-bd.sh` script that idempotently sets the custom statuses, called from `setup-git-hooks.sh` or its own one-time setup step in README/CLAUDE.md.
2. Documented as a prerequisite in `using-this-repo` skill so agents know to set them.
3. Both — script + doc.

## Fix
- `scripts/setup-bd.sh` (new): `bd config set status.custom "proposed:active,enriched:active,ready:active,in_review:wip"`, idempotent.
- Reference it from README "Quick start" and from `CLAUDE.md` "Always do first" (step 4 or new step).

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-open: branch with no commits ahead rejects PR creation
description:
## Problem
The `pr-open` recipe in `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` does:

```bash
git push -u origin "feat/$ID-$SLUG"
gh pr create --draft --base main --head "feat/$ID-$SLUG" ...
```

But a freshly-created worktree branch is identical to `main`. `gh pr create` errors: `pull request create failed: GraphQL: No commits between main and feat/...`.

## Reproduce
Every RFC 2324 MVP impl PR (ucs-n3d, ucs-4g0, ucs-23r, ucs-3fa, ucs-s0x) hit this. Workaround was a `git commit --allow-empty -m "chore(<id>): open draft PR for orchestrator tracking"` before the push.

## Fix options
1. **Empty commit before push** — bake `git commit --allow-empty -m "chore($ID): open draft PR for orchestrator tracking"` into the recipe between branch creation and `git push`. Simple, mirrors what I did manually.
2. **Skip pr-open entirely until first real commit** — move PR creation to first push of impl content. Means the issue spends part of its life with no PR URL. Bad for tracking.

Option 1 is the right tradeoff.

## Related skills to update
- `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` (the recipe text)
- `docs/specs/2026-05-18-agentic-pr-loop.md` (§4.1)

title: Orchestrator merges PRs with failing CI (no GH required checks)
description:
ADR 0005 routes branch protection through a local pre-push hook (`scripts/git-hooks/pre-push`) rather than GitHub branch protection. The pre-push hook only stops direct pushes to `main`; it does NOT keep `gh pr merge --auto` from firing when a PR's CI is red. PR #8 demonstrated this: its `lint` job failed (prettier flagged `packages/evals/src/run.ts`), but the auto-merge queue merged it anyway when the PR became "mergeable" in GitHub's eyes.

Surfaced consequence: the next PR pulling main (PR #7, ucs-n3d after rebase) inherited the prettier failure and had to absorb a cleanup commit it shouldn't have owned.

## Possible fixes
1. Configure required status checks in branch protection — re-opens the question ADR 0005 closed. Worth revisiting now that we know the cost of the alternative.
2. Replace `gh pr merge --auto --squash` in `opening-pr-orchestrator` with a polling step that asserts CI green before issuing the merge. Doable, but pushes the check into orchestrator code and skips for non-orchestrator merges.
3. Both: a script-level guard now (option 2) plus the right branch-protection config later (option 1).

## How to reproduce
1. Create a PR whose lint job fails (e.g., introduce unformatted code).
2. `gh pr merge <num> --auto --squash`.
3. Watch CI complete with lint=FAILURE.
4. PR merges anyway.

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-merge: deletes branch held by worktree, fails noisily
description:
## Problem
The `pr-merge` recipe runs:
```bash
cd \"\$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/..\"   # main repo root
gh pr merge \"\$PR_URL\" --squash --delete-branch
...
git worktree remove \"../wt-\$ID\"
```

`gh pr merge --delete-branch` tries to delete the LOCAL branch too (after the remote merge), but the local branch is still checked out in `../wt-\$ID`. Result every time:
```
failed to delete local branch feat/...: error: cannot delete branch '...' used by worktree at '/Users/sara/Projects/wt-...'
```

The merge itself works (remote is deleted, PR is closed), but the error message is noisy and the local branch sticks around until `git worktree remove ../wt-\$ID` and then `git branch -D ...`.

## Fix
Reorder the recipe:
```bash
git worktree remove \"../wt-\$ID\" --force      # before gh merge --delete-branch
gh pr merge \"\$PR_URL\" --squash --delete-branch
```

Or drop `--delete-branch` from gh and do `git push origin --delete feat/...` after worktree removal — cleaner.

Either way, the worktree must be removed BEFORE the local branch is deleted. Current recipe does it after.

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-ready: GNU 'date -Is' is non-portable
description:
## Problem
The `pr-ready` recipe in `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` records the review-pass timestamp via:

```bash
bd update "$ID" --append-note "review-pass:$N — submitted by impl-team @ \$(date -Is)"
```

macOS BSD `date` rejects `-Is` (it's a GNU extension). Result on macOS: `date: invalid argument 's' for -I`, and the bd note ends with a blank timestamp.

## Repro
On macOS:
```
$ date -Is
date: invalid argument 's' for -I
```

## Fix
Replace `\$(date -Is)` with `\$(date -u +%FT%TZ)` — portable across GNU and BSD, prints ISO 8601 UTC.

## Files
- `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` (one line in pr-ready)
